brief: Warning signs you don't need funding. Profitability, growth rate, customer love, optionality — read these before you take the meeting.

slots.scriptTagline: The warning signs every founder ignores too easily.

slots.body: If your bank account climbs every month without outside capital, you already have the only fuel you need. Profitability means control. Keep it.
Double-digit organic growth beats vanity metrics fueled by burn. If customers are arriving faster than you can serve them, a check will only dilute what is already working.
Net Promoter scores through the roof and inbound referrals mean your moat is real. Investor money cannot buy authentic word of mouth. Protect the love.
Bootstrapping keeps your cap table clean and your exit paths wide. You can sell, stay private, or pivot without asking permission. That freedom is worth more than cash.
One pitch deck often leads to six months of reporting theater. If the business is healthy, the best term sheet is the one you never sign. Think twice.
Chasing checks pulls you away from the team and the product for months. The opportunity cost is stealthy but massive. Build instead of begging.

slots.headline: BUILD ON YOUR TERMS
slots.scriptTagline: Own every decision from day one.
